name: Afghanistan
rule: The 2017 Plant Protection and Quarantine Law, Article 3(7), includes manufactured plant products only where their natural or processed form can introduce/spread plant pests. The 2019 regulation requires import permits and origin phytosanitary certificates for regulated products (Articles 6 and 22); its small personal exemption names decorative plants/flowers and fresh or dried fruits up to 2 kg, not tea. No current determination placing finished sencha inside or outside the risk-based definition was located.
personalMailApplicability: The 2019 regulation section 3(2)(7) covers goods transported for trade or other purposes, and section 4(1) includes consumption. Personal use therefore does not remove covered products from scope. The 2017 Act Article 11 authorizes discretionary permit exemptions for certain personal/research imports; it is not an automatic exemption for every small parcel.

rule: Agricultural Quarantine Law 76/2012 as amended in 2020 defines plants as living plants/parts and plant products as products processed without changing their biological nature. Article 9(2) expressly waives import licensing only for specified seed samples. No official finished-sencha classification or tea permit waiver was established.
personalMailApplicability: The 10 kg certificate exemption explicitly includes mail and commodities not intended for agricultural purposes. Applying that class to drinking tea is an inference; it does not establish an unrestricted postal route.
